name: wikijs
summary: Modern documentation and knowledge-base platform for structured content, collaboration, and searchable internal references.
why_it_matters: Wiki.js preserves useful knowledge-platform capability knowledge, but there is no current validated project workflow that justifies active maintenance as a supported resource.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs a self-hosted knowledge base or wiki.
Operators want searchable documentation with structured content workflows.
The workflow depends on a collaborative knowledge platform rather than static docs alone.

platform_support.notes: The app is containerizable, but real support depends on persistence, auth, and content-backup workflows.

prerequisites: Persistent database and content storage strategy
Defined content backup and restore workflow
implementation_notes: Promotion should validate a real documentation workflow, not only basic startup.
Keep content-management support narrower than broad wiki customizations.
Backups and exports need explicit conventions.
operational_notes: Persistence and backup quality matter more than initial setup.
Validation should include content creation and retrieval.
Auth integration changes the support surface materially.
risks: Knowledge platforms are easy to add and easy to leave unused.
A wrapper can imply stronger operational maturity than exists.
